newsitem.title: GERMANY: N.Europe rapeseed tightness offset by weak demand.
newsitem.headline: N.Europe rapeseed tightness offset by weak demand.

text.p: Northern Europe rapeseed prices were steady as supply tightness failed to impress markets paralysed by the absence of consumers, brokers said on Friday.
"Trades are thin because farmers and co-operatives are holding on to the material, but consumers won't buy at current prices because crush margins are unattractive," one said.
"In my opinion, our rape oil price is too high and if that doesn't change, producers will see prices collapse in the first half of 1997."
With oil export demand lacking and a huge feedgrain harvest just arriving at silos, there was little incentive for crushers to process seed into oil and meal.
But prices were underpinned by consumer opposition to genetically-modified U.S. soybeans, which could make consumers favour rape products.
Environmentalist and consumer groups have expressed health and environmental concerns about the new products.
They demand anything from a total ban to a segregation of altered and traditional soybeans, or at least clear labelling.
November-January rape oil cif Rotterdam was at a $4.50 premium over soy oil at $100/100 kg today, which traders attributed to demand shifts in favour of the rapeseed complex.
"We have to deal with the concerns, but in my opinion, it is a purely German campaign and it will be over in six months, once the U.S. show they won't be blackmailed," one said.
Further price support came from underlying Scandinavian and Polish crusher demand and reports that the EU rapeseed crop was some 1.3 million tonnes lower this year at 6.9 million.
But traders said large world sunseed supplies would help ease possible shortages.
Buyers free Hamburg kept October seed steady on the week at 472.50 marks, with fob Baltic port buyers at 470 marks.
Rapeseed buyers at German delivery points other than Hamburg pegged October at 457-475 marks and maintained a steady 475 marks cif in the Amsterdam-Rotterdam-Antwerp range.
The November position on the Paris Matif futures exchange was last in an untraded 473-476 marks range.
Sellers prices of local rape meal (34 percent protein) were a touch firmer, with September/October and November/January meal each 0.25 marks higher at 29.00-29.25 marks and 29.00 marks respectively.
October rape oil was steady on the week at 86.75 marks/100 kg, while November-January rape oil, at 89.00 marks, was down 0.50.
